title: `upper`, `lower`: Unicode's simple one-to-one case mappings
verdict: `char_set: UTF8` with simple mappings; sverify guards non-ASCII text
description: `upper` and `lower` map each code point on its own with utf8proc's simple case mappings, so the length never changes: `upper('ß')` is `ẞ` (U+1E9E), `upper('straße')` is `STRAẞE`, `upper('ﬁ')` stays `ﬁ`, `lower('İ')` is `i` (one character), and `lower('ΣΑΣ')` is `σασ`, with no final sigma. Accented Latin and Greek letters map as expected (`éÿ` → `ÉŸ`, `ÀΩ` → `àω`); `ǆ` uppercases to `Ǆ`.
reference: `upper`, `lower` with `char_set: UTF8` are black boxes defined as Rust's `str::to_uppercase` and `to_lowercase`: full mappings, which can change the length (`ß` → `SS`, `ﬁ` → `FI`, `İ` → `i̇`) and use a final sigma (`σας`). On ASCII text the two agree.
The written SQL raises on non-ASCII text for every engine (`ascii_only`, #70), so DuckDB never returns its mapping there. ST-10 records that Substrait's `UTF8` does not say which Unicode mapping.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe observations (duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64; session duckdb-characterization-gaps)

evidence.note: Utf8Proc::CodepointToUpper / CodepointToLower, one code point at a time (lines 45, 62)
